answer: Decaying activity escrow. Each identity posts a small refundable deposit; it earns withdrawal rights only through spaced, unpredictable liveness challenges. Missed challenges trigger a vault lock that delays release while burning a fraction of the deposit. Because a single operator must answer every clone's challenges, marginal cost scales linearly with fleet size. Cheap duplication becomes unprofitable once challenge density exceeds labor capacity. An echo of past activity also expires, forcing fresh work. The falcon challenge schedule is deliberately erratic, so batching fails.
